stories.Headline: US data vendors are selling about $500 million of AI training data, including RL environments, to Chinese labs, ChinaTalk finds
stories.Summary:
ChinaTalk, the China-tech newsletter, reported on November 11, 2026 that American AI data companies are selling roughly half a billion dollars of training data to Chinese AI labs. The findings, from an investigation by Aqib Zakaria and Quinn Ennis, include reinforcement-learning environments, which are simulated versions of apps and tasks with grading rubrics that labs use to post-train models in fields such as coding, finance, law, cyber and biology. The authors say they identified at least nine US vendors selling to Chinese customers. They relied on anonymous sources and on subcontractors, often based in India, who list client names on LinkedIn or in résumés.

The report names Mercor, Surge AI, Turing, AfterQuery, Abundant, Pareto, DeccanAI, Eaglepoint and Invisible among the vendors. Buyers cited include Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, Moonshot AI and Z.ai. ChinaTalk says data it accessed shows Mercor sold software-engineering environments to Alibaba, and it cites a Forbes report that 2 percent of Mercor's second-quarter 2026 revenue came from China. It did not publish a breakdown of the half-billion-dollar figure, and the companies' responses were not included. The only firms the authors know of that publicly say they forgo China business are Scale, micro1 and Fleet.

The authors argue that Chinese labs are buying the same environments already sold to Anthropic or OpenAI, which lets them confirm the data works and skip costly failed training runs. Surge AI's website markets its environments as "built by the same experts behind our frontier-lab work." The authors say this, combined with distillation from US models, lets Chinese labs narrow the gap with less compute of their own, and that the savings matter most because Chinese chips are short of high-bandwidth memory. They also say Mercor narrowed its customer policy in May 2026 from an ownership test to a location test.

Current US export controls cover advanced chips and some model weights, but ChinaTalk says RL environments are largely free from those controls except for Entity-Listed buyers such as Zhipu, and that an unlisted affiliate outside China can sidestep them. The authors propose that the Bureau of Industry and Security treat dual-use environments under existing rules on chips, cyber and bioweapons, and send "is-informed" letters to vendors. They also suggest the Department of War use procurement rules to bar its contractors from selling to concerning Chinese labs. The authors describe the trade as "not apocalyptic," since Chinese buyers must wait for US labs to commission an environment first, which keeps them months behind.

Articles.Title: US data vendors are selling about $500 million of AI training data, including RL environments, to Chinese labs, ChinaTalk finds - MLQ.ai

stories.Headline: Mercor's Brendan Foody: AI Will Automate Half of Digital Work, But the Real Bottleneck Is Measurement
stories.Summary:
Mercor co-founder and co-CEO Brendan Foody argued that the main constraint on AI progress is now measurement rather than model capability. He made the remarks on the MTS podcast after Mercor raised $750 million in a Series D at a $20 billion valuation. Foody's comments came in an interview published on November 11, 2026, in which he described the gap between what models can do and what anyone can yet verify. He said the barrier to automating much of the economy is finding ways to evaluate the work involved.

The article says Mercor's new funding will expand its customer base toward mainstream enterprises that want to build their own evaluations and post-train their own models. Foody described a two-phase adoption path, with evaluations coming first to establish ground truth and post-training second to improve performance on specific work. He named Harvey, Sierra and Cognition as top AI startups already in the second phase, with post-trained models in production. Most classic enterprise software companies, he said, have completed or nearly completed the first phase. He said companies typically begin building evaluations once inference spending on an agent deployment exceeds $10 million a year.

Foody is the company's co-founder and co-CEO, and the article presents his remarks as his own view of the field. He said Mercor went from near zero to roughly $3 billion in annual revenue in 27 months. He predicted that more than half of digital tasks would be automated within a few years, while physical work and tasks requiring tacit knowledge would remain harder to automate. He said the Apex accounting benchmark launched in February 2026, when frontier models scored about 23 percent, and that they now score roughly 80 percent. He also said Mercor spends three times as much on LLM inference as on employee salaries.

Other figures in the article describe how Mercor runs its own operations and how its evaluations are used. Mercor runs agents that have conducted more than 7 million candidate interviews, and an AI project manager handles about 70 percent of the actions involved in managing its hundreds of thousands of contractors. The article says Mercor sweeps its evaluations whenever a new open-source model ships and selects the best performer for each deployment. Foody said the market for Mercor's work is bounded by the number of tasks a human can do in a domain that a model cannot. He also said models have yet to improve on collaboration with other people, which he called the largest area without progress.

The article gives background on Foody's view of the field through the benchmarks Mercor co-builds with its customers, including Frontier Code with Cognition, TauBench with Sierra, LAB with Harvey, and RAMP with Apex Accounting. It notes that the Apex benchmark took roughly nine months to move from 23 percent to 80 percent. Foody said that once an evaluation exists, lab reinforcement learning can saturate it, which shortens the useful life of any single evaluation. The article also cites a host's mention of a model from a lab called NeoLab optimized for human collaboration, which Foody said he was not familiar with.

Looking ahead, Foody expects major progress in the collaboration area over the next year and said he expects task production to become more conversational and model-driven. The article does not say how quickly that change will arrive or how it would affect Mercor's business. It also does not say whether the enterprise shift to post-training will reach Fortune 500 production workloads on any particular timeline. Foody's split forecast leaves open how much of the work outside the long tail will be automated, and the article gives no further detail on that question.

Articles.Title: Mercor's Brendan Foody: AI Will Automate Half of Digital Work, But the Real Bottleneck Is Measurement - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models
stories.Summary:
Multi-vector embedding models keep many vectors per document, which lets each query token find its own match, but storage costs grow quickly at scale. Token pooling reduces those costs by merging similar token vectors, though aggressive compression can discard useful information. Pooling-aware training addresses this by teaching the encoder to preserve the information that matters when its vectors are merged. The method was described in a Hugging Face post dated November 11, 2026, written by Tom Aarsen. The post builds on pooling-aware training studied in work by Stefan Josef and by LightOn.

With pool_factor=4, a normally trained model retained 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10 while cutting document vectors fourfold. Pooling-aware training raised that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget. The post's example arithmetic shows that 200 vectors of 128 dimensions at 4-bit residual quantization need 12.8 KB per document, or 12.8 GB across a million documents. Pooling each document to 50 vectors reduces that figure to 3.2 GB. HierarchicalTokenPooling groups similar token embeddings using Ward hierarchical clustering, and it protects the first token from merging by default.

Pooling applies only to document embeddings, leaving queries unchanged, and adaptive pooling can use a shared distance threshold instead of a fixed factor. A calibration function, calibrate_distance_threshold, can set that threshold for a target average of 16 vectors per document. The training objective combines the original retrieval loss with a pooled-representation loss, weighting each at one half. The training is implemented in Sentence Transformers through MultiVectorTokenPoolingLoss, which wraps CachedMultiVectorMultipleNegativesRankingLoss.

Gradients from pooled vectors pass back to their member tokens through a straight-through estimator. The example uses a mini-batch size of 64 and a training batch size of 256. The complete script, training_cached_contrastive.py, can be run locally with uv or on a cloud GPU through Hugging Face Jobs. The Jobs example uses an A10G GPU with a four-hour time limit, and it can upload the trained model to the user's Hub account.

Articles.Title: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models

stories.Headline: U.S. Stocks Plunge in Unprecedented AI Panic Selling
stories.Summary:
On November 5, 2026, New York stocks fell sharply in what the article calls unprecedented AI-driven selling. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed at 24,315.00, down 1,421.52 points, or 5.52%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,833.06 points, or 3.44%, to 51,523.06. The Standard & Poor's 500 dropped 334.89 points, or 4.36%, to 7,353.73. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 declines were the steepest since April 2 of last year, when Trump announced reciprocal tariffs.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.25% to 9,011.14, its biggest drop since a 15.90% fall on March 16, 2020. The index closed below the 10,000 line for the first time since April 28. Nvidia's value shrank to $4.3765 trillion, widening its gap with Apple, which remained above $5 trillion. Shares of AI infrastructure firms such as CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN also fell for a second straight day.

The article says the selling was driven by fears that Democratic governors will restrict AI data center construction. Democrats won governorships in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, states where many new data center projects are planned. Goldman Sachs estimated that about 45% of planned U.S. data center expansion capacity could be affected by the Democratic victory. Some estimates put scrapped projects at roughly 10 to 15%, and Wall Street expects at least 10 to 15 gigawatts of capacity due online next year could sit idle.

Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa, elected governor, pledged an immediate moratorium on approvals for new data center construction, saying data centers are depleting residents' drinking water and raising electricity bills. Senator-elect James Talarico of Texas pledged to end tax breaks for data center developers, and Ohio Senator-elect Sherrod Brown pledged to work for voters rather than data centers or Wall Street. According to Ballotpedia data cited by Politico and CNBC, residents voted against development in 40 of 41 data center referendums across 10 states. Elon Musk, who gave $446 million to Republicans in the midterms, saw SpaceX stock fall to $123.62, below its $135 IPO price, and the combined market value of SpaceX and Tesla lost $370 billion this week.

Oil prices were also volatile, with Brent and WTI rebounding about 3.88% and 2.72% on November 5 after falling more than 8% the previous day. Ten-year Treasury yields fell 0.049 percentage point to 4.843%, and gold rose 0.99% to $4,113.50 per troy ounce. According to CME FedWatch, the odds of a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting fell to 70.9% from 82.7%. The article notes that investor sentiment could also weigh on AI company IPOs planned by Anthropic and OpenAI.

JonesTrading chief market strategist Michael O'Rourke said a slowdown in data center investment driven by political change will materialize and that earnings estimates behind the bull case are no longer valid. Bill Ackman told CNBC on November 3 that stocks were trading at prices that make no sense. Other analysts disagreed, with Natixis's Mabrouk Chetouane arguing the Democrats will not halt AI policies given the U.S.-China competition, and RWA Wealth Partners' Joseph Edmund Powers calling the concerns somewhat exaggerated. Powers said the burden on state governments will grow but will not greatly affect existing projects. Some predict Democratic governors will pursue alternative regulations or conditional approvals instead of outright bans.

Articles.Title: U.S. Stocks Plunge in Unprecedented AI Panic Selling - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Job Seekers Cram AI Skills, but Firms Say Basics Suffice
stories.Summary:
Seven to eight out of ten South Korean job seekers believe artificial intelligence skills matter when applying for jobs, yet only two in ten companies formally assess those skills during hiring. The Federation of Korean Industries released the findings on the 10th, based on a survey of 500 university students in their third year or above and 200 companies among the country's top 1,000 firms by revenue. Of the job seekers, 77.0% said AI skills are important for landing a job, while 15.2% called them of average importance and 7.8% said they were not important. The survey showed a clear gap in expectations between the two groups.

Among the companies, 39.0% said they place significant weight on AI skills when hiring entry-level staff, another 39.0% rated them of average importance, and 22.0% said they were not important. Only 20.0% include AI skills as a formal item in hiring evaluations, while 43.0% consider them only if applicants raise them voluntarily and 37.0% ignore them entirely. The two sides also disagreed on the proficiency needed. Of the job seekers, 54.8% said candidates must be able to verify and revise AI output or redesign work processes with AI, but only 18.0% of companies set either level as the minimum for new hires.

Most companies set a lower bar. A combined 67.5% cited either task application, meaning using AI to produce work for a specific business purpose (39.0%), or basic use such as searching, summarizing and drafting (28.5%). Another 14.5% said they do not require AI skills at all. Kwon Hyuk-min, head of the growth strategy division at the Federation of Korean Industries, said job seekers should focus on gaining experience applying AI to their majors and job functions rather than mastering advanced technology. He also said university education needs to shift toward practical training tied to majors and specific job roles.

Articles.Title: Job Seekers Cram AI Skills, but Firms Say Basics Suffice - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Bloomberg, JPMorgan See Korea Growing Faster Than 3.1% Next Year on AI Spending
stories.Summary:
The Korea Institute of Finance has projected that South Korea's real gross domestic product will grow 3.8% this year and 3.1% next year, which would mark a second straight year of growth above 3%. The forecast was presented by Kim Hyun-tae, head of the macroeconomic research division, at the 2027 Economic and Financial Outlook Seminar held at the Bank Hall in Seoul on the 10th. Export growth is expected to slow next year because of a high base, but domestic demand is expected to keep recovering. That recovery is seen as driven by strong facility investment, a gradual pickup in private consumption and expansionary fiscal management.

Several other forecasters were more optimistic than the institute. Kwon Hyo-sung, an economist at Bloomberg, said he expects growth of around the mid-3% range next year, on the view that demand for memory chips, Korea's most important sector, will hold up. He named the AI revolution, the war in Iran and interest rates as the three factors that will shape the global economy. Park Suk-gil, an economist at JPMorgan, said he sees upside risks to both growth and facility investment compared with the institute's outlook. The Bank of Korea, for its part, had forecast 2.9% growth for next year in its August economic outlook.

The forecasts are the views of the economists and institutions named, and the articles do not describe any policy measure or legal requirement arising from them. Kwon said the Democratic Party's victory in the recent U.S. midterm elections has raised the possibility of regulation on data centers, but he argued that projects already under way will not be affected. Kim Young-joo, head of the macroeconomic forecasting department at the Bank of Korea's Research Department, cautioned that the chip-led boom could prove a double-edged sword, since overall growth becomes more sensitive to swings in the semiconductor cycle. Lim Hong-ki, director of the economic analysis division at the Ministry of Finance and Economy's Economic Policy Bureau, said next year's policy motto is to let growth spread beyond semiconductors to other sectors.

Articles.Title: Bloomberg, JPMorgan See Korea Growing Faster Than 3.1% Next Year on AI Spending - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Hyundai Steel Honors 5 Top AI Projects From Raw Materials to Sales
stories.Summary:
Hyundai Steel gave awards to five projects at its 2026 AX Results Sharing Meeting, which it held recently at the research center of its Dangjin steel mill, and the steelmaker announced the event on November 11. The meeting was meant to share the artificial intelligence transformation results that employees pursued over the past year and to identify and spread best practices. A call for AX cases that began in August drew 198 submissions, including 58 in manufacturing and 140 in business operations. Hyundai Steel selected 48 for display and held on-site presentations and demonstrations for 15 of the strongest cases. Judges and employees at the event chose five of the presented projects as top performers.

In manufacturing, two projects were named top: a raw material logistics optimization guide tool and a guidance system for optimizing scrap raw material blending. Both were recognized for using AI to improve logistics operations and raw material blending efficiency, which contributed to higher productivity. In the business AX category, three cases were judged to have supported data-driven decision-making and improved work efficiency. These were an AI-based product sales strategy and decision-support system, agent-based automation of material procurement and coil transfer tasks, and an AI analysis framework for appropriate purchasing prices. Starting this year, the company also ran a platform that lets any employee register an AX case, take part in evaluations directly, and exchange views.

Hyundai Steel President Lee Bo-ryong said the meeting is not only an occasion to award individual projects but also a turning point at which AI spreads across the entire organization. He said successful experiences in using AX must be shared, and that the company must work together to produce tangible results that raise productivity and manufacturing competitiveness. The company has held an AI and big data festival since 2021 to spread and embed a culture of using AI. From this year, it turned that festival into the AX Results Sharing Meeting to accelerate results aimed at upgrading its steel manufacturing competitiveness.

Articles.Title: Hyundai Steel Honors 5 Top AI Projects From Raw Materials to Sales - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: iL Joins Korea Physical AI Association to Expand Partnerships
stories.Summary:
iL, a company that operates a data platform for physical artificial intelligence, has become a full member of the Korea Physical AI Association, the company said on November 11, 2026. The firm had earlier joined ADRA, a major European body covering AI, data and robotics, as an official member. The Korea Physical AI Association is an industry cooperation group licensed by the Ministry of Science and ICT that links companies and research institutes across AI, robotics, data and manufacturing. Its work includes industrial field testing, data standardization, joint research and development, and building a physical AI industry ecosystem. The membership strengthens iL's ties with the physical AI industry at home and abroad.

iL has gathered operational data on tasks, movement and responses to obstacles by running humanoid robots at actual industrial sites. In September, the company recorded its first revenue in the business from a contract to supply humanoid robots and physical AI data. The company plans to use the membership to widen cooperation with domestic industry, academia and research institutes. It also intends to work with ADRA's European network on international joint research, data standardization and global industrial field testing. The company frames these moves as a way to test the potential of a business model built on operational data.

Jung Moon-sik, chief AI officer at iL, said the core competitiveness of physical AI lies in securing operational data generated at industrial sites and linking it to AI training and performance gains. He said the company will keep building global competitiveness on technology verified at domestic sites and on its experience commercializing data. He also said the memberships in Europe's ADRA and the Korea Physical AI Association will expand its cooperation networks at home and abroad. His stated goal is for iL to become a physical AI operational data platform company that represents South Korea.

Articles.Title: iL Joins Korea Physical AI Association to Expand Partnerships - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on November 11, 2026, a next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations affect specific human cell types. The model is designed to give scientists a new tool for finding the cellular drivers of disease. The announcement was authored by Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec. Its aim is to bridge single-cell biology and human genetics by predicting how hundreds of human cell types respond to genetic variants.

AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model that predicts DNA effects for one tissue, cell type or state at a time, rather than predicting many tissues in parallel. It takes a million-letter DNA sequence along with a target biological condition, chosen from a reference catalog or generated from a scientist's own single-cell experiment through a cell encoder. The model was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues, and it also predicts DNA methylation. On the TenK10K dataset of 28 primary immune cell types, it identified nearly twice as many causal variants as the earlier model, at 30% against 16%. It is available today for non-commercial research through the AlphaGenome API and in private preview for commercial research.

Google DeepMind is responsible for building the model, and the company said it reconfigured the architecture to treat cell types differently from the first AlphaGenome. The announcement said the redesign lets the model learn how the same stretch of DNA is read differently across cell types. Google DeepMind also said that a single measurement, such as single-cell gene activity, can let the model predict unmeasured properties such as chromatin accessibility. The company described the model as a step-change improvement in variant predictive performance.

Professor Sarah Teichmann, co-founder of the Human Cell Atlas consortium and Professor of Stem Cell Medicine at the University of Cambridge, was quoted in the announcement. Peter Donnelly, CEO of Genomics Limited, said the company plans to incorporate the model into its Mystra platform and called it an impressive advance. The announcement said researchers studying inflammatory bowel disease can use the model to reproduce a finding that a variant boosts the ETS2 gene in gut macrophages. It also said the model predicted that a variant linked to severe COVID-19 disrupts gene activity more strongly in activated immune cells.

The first AlphaGenome was launched last year, and Google DeepMind later expanded it with AlphaGenome Atlas, which contains predictions for all 9 billion possible single-letter changes in the human genome. The announcement also said the Human Cell Atlas is mapping gene expression for millions of cells. Google DeepMind said it precomputed AlphaGenome 2 predictions for trait-associated variants across hundreds of human cell and tissue conditions. The company said the predictions cover traits ranging from height to type 2 diabetes.

Google DeepMind said it will continue working with researchers at the Wellcome Sanger Institute to profile a wider range of human cell types, developmental lineages and perturbed cellular states. It said it will soon release AlphaGenome 2 Skills in Google Antigravity, its agentic development platform. The company asked researchers to submit use cases by November 30, and said selected projects may be eligible for additional quota and credits. The articles do not say how the commercial private preview will be priced or when it will open more widely, and they give no independent validation of the model's results beyond the company's own benchmarks.

Articles.Title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease

stories.Headline: 'Huang Scandal' Widens as Republicans Join Call to Halt AI Chip Exports to China
stories.Summary:
The fallout from an extramarital affair scandal involving Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang is spreading quickly in Washington. Both the Democratic Party and the governing Republican Party have called for immediate export controls on artificial intelligence chips bound for China, and related legislation has begun moving fast. Democrats are directing their criticism at the Commerce Department and other relevant agencies, as well as at President Donald Trump, who has defended Huang. The reporting, which first appeared on November 10, 2026, describes a widening political reaction that centers on the affair and on concerns about chips reaching China.

Sen. Jim Banks, a Republican from Indiana, and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, issued a joint statement on the 9th. They said the Commerce Department must close loopholes in AI chip export controls and act immediately to keep advanced chips from reaching the Chinese military. They also urged Congress to pass key measures, including AI surveillance provisions in the National Defense Authorization Act, so that China's routes to advanced semiconductors can be blocked. One proposal would bar exports to China of chips more advanced than Nvidia's H200 for a set period. Reuters reported that the defense bill could also require companies to track where semiconductors are located, and include the MATCH Act, which would restrict allied countries from exporting chipmaking equipment to China.

Three Republican House committee chairmen, Brian Mast of Florida, John Moolenaar of Michigan and Rick Crawford of Arkansas, sent Huang a letter on the 4th. They asked him to respond by the 11th on whether he would attend a closed-door briefing on the 18th. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, a Democrat from New York and the leading candidate for the next House speaker, said at a news conference that he would work to include the chip export restriction bills in the defense authorization act. The reconciled version of the defense bill could reach the floor in the second week of December, with a vote and presidential signature possibly coming after mid-December.

The reporting places this push in a broader debate over U.S.-China technology competition. A former senior U.S. official, speaking to foreign correspondents in Washington on the same day, said the Nvidia situation would become a significant problem going forward. That official also signaled that some restrictions could emerge on certain types of economic and technological exchange between the United States and China. The articles do not say whether Huang will attend the briefing or whether the restrictions will be enacted in their proposed form.

Articles.Title: 'Huang Scandal' Widens as Republicans Join Call to Halt AI Chip Exports to China - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: One in Three Young Americans Turns to AI for Drug Information
stories.Summary:
One in three young adults in the United States has used generative artificial intelligence to look up information about drugs, according to a survey reported by Seoul Economic Daily on November 8, 2026. A research team led by Dr. Mireia Triguero Lloura of the Center for Pharmacoepidemiology at Rutgers University surveyed 995 men and women aged 18 to 29 living in the United States in April 2026 through the online research platform Prolific. Participants were recruited in equal proportions by age and gender, with race matched to the young adult population. The paper was published on the 19th of the latest issue of the journal JMIR Formative Research. The team set out to examine how often young adults use generative AI for drug information and how they judge the answers they receive.

Of the respondents, 32.3 percent, or 321 people, said they had used AI for drug information, and 48.2 percent of those users did so at least once a month. In the same survey, 57.5 percent, or 572 people, said they had searched Google for drug-related information, a higher share than those using AI. Asked about their purposes in a multiple-response question, 92.8 percent cited checking the risks and consequences of drug use, while 48.6 percent cited information about the drugs themselves, such as dosage. Men reported AI use at 39.8 percent compared with 24.8 percent for women, and Black respondents reported 51.1 percent compared with 29.8 percent for white respondents. On a five-point scale, respondents rated their average trust in AI answers about drugs at 3.66, higher than the 3.51 they gave for general use.

The research team said large language models operate on probability and can repeat incorrect information, and it called for further research into the accuracy of the answers and how young adults interpret and act on them. The survey did not assess whether the AI answers were accurate. The team also cautioned that its online non-probability sample may have included many respondents already familiar with AI, which could inflate usage rates. The paper cited a January 5 report by SFGate that a California teenager who had sought drug advice from AI died of an overdose. The article notes that the quotes from foreign sources were based on Korean-language reports and may not reflect exact original wording.

Articles.Title: One in Three Young Americans Turns to AI for Drug Information - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Pulmuone Taps AI and Robots for Food Production With 11 Startups
stories.Summary:
Pulmuone, a South Korean food company, said on November 11, 2026 that it is expanding partnerships with startups to apply artificial intelligence and robotics to food production and quality control. The announcement followed its "2026 Pulmuone Open Innovation Demo Day," held October 10 at its Suseo headquarters in Seoul's Gangnam district, where it presented results from technology collaborations with 11 startups. The event, now in its fourth year, showcased projects carried out by Pulmuone's business units and its research institute together with those startups. Five of the projects focused on AI transformation, four on smart agriculture and blue technology, and two on sustainable food.

The collaborations covered a wide range, from consumer research and customized marketing to manufacturing automation, food quality control and new ingredient development. With Robotable, the company looked at deploying collaborative and humanoid robots in food manufacturing. With Datasketchers, it tested AI that detects quality and food safety risks in the supply chain in advance. Other projects included a robot-automated vertical farm for baby leaf production with Lowain, plant-based food development using water lentil with Byroot, and efforts to raise harvest yields for green juice ingredients and to make materials from food byproducts.

Three of the 11 projects were carried out under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups' public-private open innovation support program, and Pulmuone funded the other eight itself. Pulmuone said grand prize and excellence award winners will be chosen through evaluations by internal and external experts. Winners will receive follow-up support including prize money and mentoring. Startups with strong commercialization potential may get additional collaboration or strategic investment.

Chief executive Lee Woo-bong said he hopes the results will serve as a starting point for discovering new growth together and carrying it into actual businesses. The company has run its startup cooperation program with the Seoul Center for Creative Economy and Innovation since 2023. About 300 startups applied for collaboration last year, and the number of companies taking part in proof-of-concept projects rose to 10 from four in 2024. The articles do not describe the outcomes of the projects or name any specific commercial deployments.

Articles.Title: Pulmuone Taps AI and Robots for Food Production With 11 Startups - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: U.S. Stocks Fall on Rate-Hike Fears; Nvidia Slips to No. 3 by Market Value
stories.Summary:
U.S. stock indexes all fell on November 10, 2026, after a hotter-than-expected October consumer price index raised the odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase in December. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 52,231.89, down 157.86 points or 0.30%, while the S&P 500 ended at 7,520.93, down 0.38%. The Nasdaq Composite finished at 25,065.87, down 187.26 points or 0.74%. Stocks opened lower after the October CPI was released before the opening bell, and they stayed down for the session. Nvidia dropped 5.47%, and at one point it slipped behind Microsoft to third place by market value.

The U.S. Labor Department said the all-items CPI rose 0.4% in October from September on a seasonally adjusted basis, above expectations of a 0.3% increase. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% from the previous month, against forecasts of a 0.2% gain. According to CME FedWatch, the probability of a rate increase at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting rose to 100% from 84.0% a day earlier. The odds of a 0.50 percentage point increase rose to 11.2% from 0%. Nvidia has lost $400 billion, about 540 trillion won, in market value over two days.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said at a conference in London that he was leaning toward supporting a 0.25 percentage point increase at the December meeting. He said economic activity is strong and the labor market is stable, but inflation is too high and well above the FOMC's 2% target. Waller added that if October core CPI came in near or above 0.3%, the committee should consider a 0.50 percentage point increase in December. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, speaking in Houston the same day, said the pace of increases could quicken and that the FOMC should deliver at least two increases of 0.25 percentage point.

Nvidia's decline followed a scandal involving Chief Executive Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy. Huang acknowledged on the 8th that he had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed director identified as an agent of Chinese intelligence. Market participants also followed Anthropic's initial public offering, in which the company plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, raising as much as $64.4 billion. At the top of the range, Anthropic would be valued at about $1.4 trillion. Separately, it will raise $26 billion through private placements with investors including Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC.

Stocks pared losses as oil prices fell, with Brent crude for January delivery settling at $91.49 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate for December at $86.04 a barrel. Both benchmarks were at their lowest levels since August 31. Oil extended early declines on expectations that the United States and Iran would avoid military conflict. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris that a large-scale military operation against Iran was not necessary at this point. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said claims that the United States was negotiating with Iran in Qatar were entirely false.

Nvidia's slide in market value was the first time since June of last year that Microsoft had overtaken it. The Fed's rate-increase odds had already risen sharply in the days before the CPI release, as Waller and Logan spoke publicly on the same day. The articles give no further background on the Huang matter beyond the acknowledgment and the identification of Alice Huang as a former Megaspeed director. Anthropic's offering price is set for the 18th, and its Nasdaq listing is scheduled for the 19th. The articles do not say how markets will react to the December FOMC decision or whether the Anthropic offering will be priced within the range.

Articles.Title: U.S. Stocks Fall on Rate-Hike Fears; Nvidia Slips to No. 3 by Market Value - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Deel Launches AI Tool to Catch Fake Job Applicants
stories.Summary:
Deel, a global human resources and payroll platform, said on November 5, 2026, that it had launched Deel Security, an artificial intelligence-powered tool meant to prevent identity fraud in hiring. The service is designed to catch applicants who use deepfakes or steal another person's identity to get a job, and it keeps checking identities after people are hired. Deel Security assesses fraud risk using a resume, online activity history, interviews and identification documents. It can detect AI-manipulated video and cases where someone else sits in on an interview for the applicant, and it compares a live photo of the applicant's face with a government-issued ID. Identities are checked again at key security points after hiring, and the service is available in more than 150 countries.

The tool works with Deel's own applicant tracking system as well as outside systems, so corporate HR and security staff can check an applicant's fraud risk without leaving the software they already use. Applications the AI flags as high risk go to Deel's fraud response specialists for further review. The final decision rests with the client company's responsible team. Deel built the tool to address identity theft and AI-driven employment fraud, both of which have grown alongside remote hiring. The technology comes from Clarity, an AI security firm Deel acquired in July, and Deel began offering the product to customers on October 29.

Deel's co-founder and chief executive, Alex Bouaziz, said AI has made fake resumes, deepfakes and stolen identities cheaper to create and harder to spot. He said the company intends to protect other companies by verifying identities from the moment someone applies and throughout their employment. The article places the launch in a wider context: last month South Korean police opened an investigation after reports that North Korean IT workers had hidden their identities to take jobs at private companies in the country and had actually done development work. A Deel survey of 1,011 HR professionals in the United States and the United Kingdom found that 66 percent said suspicious applications for remote work had increased over the past year.

Articles.Title: Deel Launches AI Tool to Catch Fake Job Applicants - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea Backs Three Core Physical AI Parts, Targets Robot Batteries by 2030
stories.Summary:
The South Korean government will back the development of next-generation sensors and actuators for robots, along with rechargeable batteries for humanoid robots. Its stated aims are to begin mass production of domestically made actuators in 2029 and to commercialize humanoid batteries in earnest by 2030. The plan was unveiled at an emergency economic ministers' meeting held at the Government Complex Seoul on November 11, 2026. It sets out detailed tasks for three physical artificial intelligence core components that were added in July to 15 existing projects. In sensors, the government will develop chips that run AI directly at the sensor level and test them in robotics, defense and mobility, with 49.8 billion won in state funds planned from 2027 to 2030.

For actuators, the government will develop lighter products with higher output and durability and verify their performance at manufacturing sites. It has set a target of raising the localization rate for core robot components to 80% by 2030. For batteries, it will raise the output and energy density of existing cells while developing next-generation all-solid-state batteries. Next year's budget proposal includes 13.3 billion won in state funds for 18 tasks across the two areas. The plan was presented by the government as part of its Hyper-Innovation Economy Leading Project, and the articles do not name a specific official who spoke at the meeting.

The government said it will hold public-private task force meetings for each task within the year to gather industry input. The articles do not describe any objections or reactions from companies or lawmakers. The plan is a funding and targets framework rather than a finished policy, and the articles do not say how the budget will be approved or which companies will receive support. The next steps they describe are the task force meetings within the year and the upcoming budget process for next year.

Articles.Title: Korea Backs Three Core Physical AI Parts, Targets Robot Batteries by 2030 - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: ChatGPT Plus for veterans and servicemembers
stories.Summary:
OpenAI said in a November 11, 2026 post that more than 20,000 transitioning servicemembers and veterans have claimed a free year of ChatGPT Plus over the past year. The offer was made by OpenAI to these groups, and the company framed the milestone as a chance to look at how veterans are using AI to prepare for civilian careers. The effort began with veterans who work at OpenAI, who know firsthand how hard the transition can be. Beyond the free access, OpenAI Academy and community partners have hosted more than a dozen trainings for nearly 1,000 members of the military community, with seven more scheduled before the year ends.

The free year is offered through ID.me, which OpenAI credited for helping servicemembers and veterans access the offer. Veterans are using the tool to organize job searches, rehearse interviews, and explore career paths they had not considered. Air Force veteran Tilak Bhatnagar used his free year to prepare for a dozen interviews and weigh competing job offers, and he later took a role at a tech company. Air Force veteran Sadarian Bell used it to turn nearly a decade of military healthcare experience into a civilian résumé and practiced interviews aloud using voice mode. Navy veteran Kelli Ramirez used it to publish two books.

OpenAI Academy gives veterans, transitioning servicemembers, and military spouses a place to learn how to use the tools alongside people who understand their situation. The company recently completed a six-event Academy series with Veterans Forge aimed at helping veterans and military families work toward their goals. A workshop in Reston, Virginia drew nearly 100 veterans and active-duty servicemembers, and more than 80 Legionnaires attended three AI training sessions at the American Legion's national convention in Louisville, Kentucky. OpenAI said these sessions, along with workshops alongside AI Collective Hampton Roads and NPower, are shaping what it offers veterans next.

OpenAI said its goal is to help veterans and military families carry the skills they built in service into whatever work they choose next. The company is continuing this work with partners through the rest of the year, including a November 14 event in Nashville with Veterans Forge and Wounded Warrior Project. The post also thanked veterans for their service and for their contributions to their communities. Readers can check whether they are eligible for the free year of ChatGPT Plus through the company's offer page.

Articles.Title: ChatGPT Plus for veterans and servicemembers

stories.Headline: AIDeep, AXLRator to Jointly Develop Generative AI Security Solutions
stories.Summary:
AIDeep, a sub-subsidiary of KSign, announced on Nov. 9 that it has signed a memorandum of understanding with AXLRator, an artificial intelligence integration platform company, to cooperate on generative AI security technologies and joint commercialization. The two companies plan to combine AIDeep's security solution, DeepGenGuard, with AXLRator's AXL-AEP integration platform. They also intend to jointly plan and develop AI transformation solutions with stronger security features. The agreement was reported by The Elec on Nov. 10, 2026. The deal was announced through a formal signing ceremony attended by the chief executives of both firms.

The companies will run a proof of concept by next month to connect DeepGenGuard to AI service development and operating environments that use AXL-AEP. The project is designed to attach the security tool through application programming interfaces and proxies without significantly changing existing service architectures. Depending on the results, the companies plan to refine the integration technology and build the joint solutions. Separately, the two firms are working on a project under the Korea Internet and Security Agency's 2026 AI Security Promising Enterprise Development Support Program. That project aims to build a security platform that protects personal and sensitive information across the generative AI software development life cycle.

Under that project, AIDeep will supply DeepGenGuard, provide technical support and design validation scenarios. AXLRator will review the AXL-AEP integration and give operational feedback. AIDeep CEO Koo Ja-dong said the partnership will produce a security-focused AI transformation solution based on real-world needs and help expand the market. AXLRator CEO Lee Kang-jin said security is becoming a necessity as adoption of AI transformation grows, and that the combined offering will let customers use generative AI with more confidence. The article also notes that KSign, which specializes in personal information protection, sold its entire stake in AIDeep to its subsidiary SANDS Lab in March of last year, after which SANDS Lab held an 80.91 percent stake.

Articles.Title: AIDeep, AXLRator to Jointly Develop Generative AI Security Solutions - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Nvidia Plans Investments in Upstage, Motif and RealWorld
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced on November 9, 2026, that it plans to invest in three South Korean artificial intelligence startups: Upstage, Motif Technologies and RealWorld. The plans were unveiled at the Ministry of Science and ICT–Nvidia AI Startup Partnership Forum held at COEX in Seoul that day. All three companies are developing their own AI models. The report, published by The Elec on November 9, also notes that Nvidia VP Deepu Talla announced the collaboration earlier that day during the morning session of Nvidia AI Day Seoul 2026. Upstage develops the Solar series of large language models and AI tools for document processing.

In April, it raised 180 billion won in the first closing of its Series C round, and its current valuation exceeds 1 trillion won. The company is now raising more funding in a second closing of the same round. Motif Technologies develops the Motif series of large language models and completed a 24 billion won Series B round in May. It is expected to receive additional investment from existing investors and Nvidia. RealWorld, a physical AI startup, builds general-purpose foundation models for robots and has recently been raising 200 billion won, with a pre-money valuation of about 1 trillion won.

Deepu Talla leads the company's presence in these partnerships and presented the collaboration with RealWorld during the Seoul event. The article does not give further detail on the terms of each investment beyond the funding figures reported for each startup. The report places the announcements within Nvidia's broader ties to Korea. In April this year, Nvidia invested in Point2 Technology, which specializes in AI data center interconnects and developed e-Tube, a data transmission technology based on radio-frequency semiconductors and plastic waveguides. Nvidia also supports more than 1,000 South Korean startups through its Nvidia Inception program.

Articles.Title: Nvidia Plans Investments in Upstage, Motif and RealWorld - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Nota Cuts AI Inference Time by Up to 52% Using AMD GPU-NPU Combination
stories.Summary:
Nota AI, a Korean company that specializes in lightweighting and optimizing AI models, presented new results at the AMD Advancing AI World Tour Seoul 2026 event. The company said its in-house tests on the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor showed total response time cut by as much as 52%, along with a 31% drop in energy consumed per token. The findings were reported by THE ELEC on November 10, 2026. Nota also noted that it joined AMD's Robotics Partner Network in July.

The core of the technique is splitting work between the GPU and the NPU inside the same AMD chip. According to the article, the NPU handles prefill, the stage that processes input information for an AI model, while the GPU handles decode, the stage that generates the response. Nota says its approach lets both units share the same model weights, which reduces redundant memory use and improves efficiency. In tests using Alibaba's open-weight Qwen3-8B model, total response completion time fell between 28% and 52% compared with AMD's existing GPU-NPU hybrid setup. Generation time per token dropped 41% to 46%.

Nota also presented results from applying an AI agent-based optimization process to its NetsPresso platform. The agents analyze model and hardware traits, develop strategies, test performance on real devices, and refine the results automatically. Across models including Llama, Qwen, Phi and Mistral running in AMD Ryzen AI environments, the company reported memory usage down 11% to 32% compared with the same hybrid setup. Response generation was 2.5 to 3.8 times faster than with NPU-only execution. Nota said it is extending the work to runtimes and GPU kernels.

Nota's chief technology officer, Tae-ho Kim, spoke at the event, and the company said it expects the technology to reach fields including AI PCs and robotics. The article does not describe any commercial rollout dates or availability for the optimization products. It also does not report independent verification of the test results, which Nota described as in-house. Further details on deployment and third-party validation were not provided in the source material.

Articles.Title: Nota Cuts AI Inference Time by Up to 52% Using AMD GPU-NPU Combination - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: KOTRA Hosts European Semiconductor Summit in Munich
stories.Summary:
KOTRA, Korea's trade and investment promotion agency, held the "European Semiconductor Summit" in Munich, Germany, on November 10 local time, working with the Korea AI Fabless Industry Association. The event ran alongside SEMICON Europa, Europe's largest semiconductor exhibition, and brought together 60 companies, 30 from Korea in semiconductor design, equipment and parts, and 30 European manufacturers and demand companies. The summit is set to run for four days from November 10. The article presents it as a way for Korean firms to pursue cooperation with European buyers.

The rationale rests on Germany's plans to expand its digital infrastructure. According to the Federal Ministry for Digital and State Modernization, Germany intends to at least double its data center capacity and increase its artificial intelligence and high-performance computing capacity more than fourfold by 2030. That growth is expected to raise demand for computing chips as well as next-generation power semiconductors and modules that support power supply and energy efficiency. Local investment is also rising, with Infineon opening an advanced semiconductor plant in Dresden last July with a €5 billion investment.

The plant will produce power and analog/mixed-signal semiconductors for automobiles, renewable energy and artificial intelligence, which the article says creates more openings for Korean equipment and parts suppliers. KOTRA organized the summit and said it will focus on follow-up work so the event does not end as a one-off exchange. KOTRA's Europe Regional Headquarters head, Kim Yeon-jae, said Germany's demand for cooperation with Korean semiconductor companies is higher than ever amid the shift to artificial intelligence and electrification. Kim pledged that KOTRA would spare no effort in supporting K-fabless and advanced semiconductor firms so they can become long-term partners in the European supply chain.

The agency said it has analyzed European buyers' demand since March and will support local proof of concept testing and joint research and development after the summit, to help turn talks into export contracts. On the first day, participants discussed advanced chip design and manufacturing, semiconductors for future vehicles, and applying artificial intelligence in robots and automation equipment. One-on-one business consultations followed, in which companies examined product specifications, technical requirements and whether their products could work on European production lines. The article does not report any contracts signed or outcomes from those meetings.

Articles.Title: KOTRA Hosts European Semiconductor Summit in Munich - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: Samsung, AMD Join Forces to Upgrade Semiconductor Test Infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics said on November 10, 2026 (local time) that it is partnering with U.S. chipmaker AMD to upgrade the test equipment used in semiconductor manufacturing. The goal is to pair Samsung's memory and storage products with AMD's high-performance processors so that the large volumes of data produced during chip testing can be handled faster and more efficiently. The announcement came as AMD launched its EPYC Embedded 9006 Series SP7 processors that day. The collaboration centers on deploying AMD processors inside Samsung's own manufacturing test infrastructure rather than supplying Samsung memory to AMD.

The integration combines Samsung's DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM memory, its PCIe Gen 6-based PM1763 SSD, and its CXL 3.2-based CMM-D MD310 memory module with AMD's EPYC Embedded 9006 Series processors. The new processors are built on AMD's Zen 6 architecture and support up to 256 cores and 512 threads. Compared with the previous EPYC 9005 Series, they deliver up to 1.8 times higher throughput, 2.7 times greater memory bandwidth and 1.5 times higher I/O bandwidth. They also support 16 channels of DDR5 memory, up to 96 lanes of PCIe Gen 6 and CXL 3.1 connectivity. The processors are meant to improve the parallel processing of automated test equipment so that several tests can run at once.

Choi Jang-seok, vice president of Samsung Electronics' Memory Product Planning Team, said in an AMD Newsroom announcement on November 10 that manufacturing test environments must keep pace as memory and I/O technologies advance. He said combining AMD's latest processors with Samsung's memory would provide scalable computing performance, memory bandwidth and high-speed I/O, and that Samsung intends to bring these capabilities into its testing operations. Industry observers quoted in the article described the deal as more than a simple product supply arrangement. They noted that rapidly rising data transfer volumes in DRAM and SSDs could hurt production efficiency and quality checks if test equipment falls short.

AMD plans to begin shipping the 128-core model of the EPYC Embedded 9006 Series on November 15, with the rest of the lineup to follow by year's end. The processors are also aimed at enterprise storage and network firewall systems, and AMD has committed to seven years of product longevity for the series. Separately, AMD announced on November 10 that its sixth-generation EPYC server processors, also based on Zen 6, are generally available, with systems from major server makers already shipping and partnerships under way with Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The article places the Samsung collaboration within broader efforts to meet demand across AI, cloud computing and high-performance computing markets.

Articles.Title: Samsung, AMD Join Forces to Upgrade Semiconductor Test Infrastructure - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: Taiwan's GIS targets 800G/1.6T AI optics, with laser packaging ramp-up starting 4Q26
stories.Summary:
Taiwan-based GIS, a company that until now has been best known for touch displays, is moving into semiconductor optics, according to a DIGITIMES report published on November 10, 2026. The company plans to begin small-volume production of laser packaging in the fourth quarter of 2026. The report says the effort is aimed at optical components for AI systems running at 800G and 1.6T speeds. Beyond that, the available text is limited because the full article sits behind a paid subscription. The shift means the company is moving away from its traditional display business and into the optical parts that link data center hardware.

According to the report, full capacity is expected to arrive in the second or third quarter of 2027. The ramp-up is therefore planned in two stages, first a small-volume start and then a much larger output later in the following year. The visible text does not describe investment figures, customer names, or the number of production lines involved. The visible portion of the report does not name anyone at GIS who is responsible for the plan or quote any executive. It also does not say whether any regulator or partner is involved.

Because the bulk of the article is locked, further details about management statements, sourcing, or customer commitments cannot be confirmed from what is available here. The move reflects broader demand for high-speed optical links as AI computing clusters grow, which is the context the headline points to. The available text does not say how GIS's plans compare with those of competitors or what milestones follow after the 2027 capacity target. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Taiwan's GIS targets 800G/1.6T AI optics, with laser packaging ramp-up starting 4Q26 - digitimes

stories.Headline: UNLV students develop AI-powered drone to clean high-rise windows
stories.Summary:
A team of engineering students at UNLV is developing an AI-powered drone designed to clean high-rise buildings while keeping workers on the ground. The reporting was published on November 10, 2026, by FOX5 Las Vegas, with Alexis Fernandez credited as the reporter. The students are part of a startup called Gagamba, which grew out of UNLV's President's Innovation Challenge. The team is pursuing the project because window cleaning on tall buildings has long been dangerous. In a city known for its hotels and glass facades, the work typically means bringing in complicated gear, going up to the roof, and lowering workers over the side on scaffolds.

Tony Ferrar, a UNLV engineering professor, has been leading the student group, and he said the basic method for cleaning windows has barely changed in decades. He described the rigging of scaffolds as complicated and the safety issues as significant. Vaughn Guintu, a sophomore who serves as the company's CEO, said the team was asked to build a solution that used AI to benefit the Las Vegas valley. He cited OSHA records showing 88 accidents over the last 15 years, 62 of which were fatal. Guintu argued that existing technologies such as drones, computer vision, and robotics could be combined to save more lives.

The system pairs a drone with an onboard water tank, a robotic squeegee and brush system, and artificial intelligence that decides how much water each window needs. Guintu said that removing bird droppings requires far less water than cleaning window streaks, and he claimed the approach uses 29 times less water than the tethered pressure washing systems in use today. The team is building a prototype and seeking partnerships with local window-cleaning companies, which would give them a platform to prove the technology and test the data. The article says the team plans to begin testing with local businesses such as Avanti Green Eco Cleaning soon.

Its long-term goal is to become commercially viable once enough funding is secured. Guintu described the mission as saving lives by preventing avoidable deaths at height. The article does not give a launch date for commercial use or the amount of funding the team needs. It also does not say when testing with local businesses will begin beyond the word "soon."

Articles.Title: UNLV students develop AI-powered drone to clean high-rise windows
